items.title: Profile pass: a brand co-owner who promotes his clothing brand without ever making an ad
items.creator: @robertmckeaveney
items.teaches: A clothing-brand co-owner grew his personal account to 367K followers in about 11 weeks without ever making an ad: useful marketing advice and fun challenges from his own name, the brand worn in every frame, and every reel ending on his bio card (co-owner of the brand + shop link) with a 'follow' CTA, never 'buy'. His hooks are borrowed: a stitch of someone's provocation answered with a montage of receipts, proven viral formats with the niche swapped, a score counter on a challenge. Three of his six newest reels beat the average (measured by likes, because view counts are hidden when logged out). Open question on your dashboard: how to get ALL his reels.

items.title: Don't make a commercial look like a commercial: dress it as a trailer, vlog or music video
items.creator: @ginyboi
items.teaches: Ads that look like ads get skipped, because people now spend money on the culture they relate to, not on ads. So make a commercial look like something else (a movie trailer, a vlog, a music video): first understand the buyer's culture, then tell the product's story in that culture's visual language. His proof pair: a stock template coffee ad with a price and feature call-outs (the template text was never even replaced) versus an editorial photo of an exhausted office worker passed out on his desk, with only the coffee brand's wordmark on it.

items.title: Make the song an entrance: a tonal sound-effects build-up in the song's key
items.creator: @multiply.sound
items.teaches: Instead of dropping a song in at full volume, introduce it: a tonal ping, a soft pad and an instrument phrase all in the song's key, a hint of the song's own synth line, then its vocals, building until the full song lands on a tonal hit and a whoosh. The audience recognises the melody before it starts, so the song makes an entrance. The reel is also a sound company's ad dressed as a tutorial (every clip on the timeline is from their key-sorted library). Its 'three simple steps' are cut off, so the build was read off the timeline.
items.use: No note. Use: the music entry of a teaser or a cold open, landing the bed on the title card, and the first reveal of an ad; we already hold key-matched ping-boom files in the sound pack. The reel slows the vocal stem, which our no-speed-change rule forbids, so we build it at normal speed unless you allow it.

items.title: Why textures make videos look premium, and where we would add them
items.creator: @manisterrrrr
items.teaches: Texture (grain, noise, paper, halftone, pixel) is what makes show intros and big explainer channels look premium; the same graphic without it looks flat. It lists 14 search words for finding textures (halftone, grain, paper, grunge, ink, film, stone, metal and more). Why we don't use it: no rule blocks it. We only add a light film grain on the grade (amount 5 to 9, which YouTube mostly smooths away), we never added a texture step for maps, title cards, reel bands or covers, and we keep no texture files. The placement plan (app, blend mode, opacity per element) is on the shelf and waits for your yes on the decision page.
items.use: Example: on the next KaalAurKatha long-form, film grain 8 on the grade layer, a paper texture on Multiply 10% over its maps and chapter cards, a stone texture inside the title letters, and grain 6 on its reels.

items.title: Rule of thirds: the four power points and what goes where
items.creator: @aevyvideoschool
items.teaches: Split any frame into a 3×3 grid: the four crossing points are where the eye lands, because we read in a Z or F path, not from the centre. The points are not equal: top-left gets the most attention, then top-right, bottom-left and bottom-right. Put the title, face or main subject on the top-left hero spot, supporting text next down the left, and logos or credits in a weak corner. Sliding a centred subject about a quarter of the frame off centre onto a point makes the same picture feel better.
items.use: Example: KaalAurKatha covers put the hero face on an upper point and the Hindi title on the upper third line; YouTube thumbnails keep the bottom-right (under the duration badge) empty; AI shot prompts place the subject on the strongest free point.

items.title: Content funnel: half the posts for attention, half for sales
items.creator: @robertmckeaveney
items.teaches: A clothing brand's 11.7M-view entertainment reel sold less than its 46K-view product reel: the first is where people discover you, the second is where they buy. His chart: a content mix turned 100,000 views into 1,000 sales (1%), a feed of only product posts turned 5,000 views into 250 (5%), so the mix sold 4× more. Rule: half the content wins attention so the other half can convert it. For us: pair every promo reel that sends viewers to a long-form video with at least one discovery reel that only hooks.
items.use: Shared untitled, so routed by content: plan KaalAurKatha reels as discovery + promo pairs per long-form video (story hook reels for reach, promo cuts with the link band for clicks). Same creator as the profile you asked to analyse (row N1).

items.title: Voice-note idea capture: voice note, transcript, linked notes
items.creator: @aevyvideoschool
items.teaches: The creator never tries to remember an idea: each one goes as a WhatsApp voice note to an AI contact, a model on his PC turns it into text, and Obsidian links it into a web of ideas. Our studio already does this for reels (share, transcribe, linked brain, dashboard graph). The one missing piece is your own spoken ideas. A free route: record in the Pixel Recorder app and share its transcript to the Notion Idea Box.
items.use: Shared untitled, so routed by content: a voice-note path into the Idea Box for story ideas you have on the go, cleaned into a row on the next capture.

items.title: Avocado vs 1,000 cuts: dicing into counted cubes in Blender (Geometry Nodes)
items.creator: @infiniteslice01
items.teaches: Yes, this can be made in Blender for free, with no add-ons: Geometry Nodes fills the avocado with a 3D grid of tiny cubes, every knife pass leaves a slice line, and once the third direction is cut the cubes fall into a pile while two counters (cuts and cubes) count up. The cube number is real maths, about (cuts / 3) cubed times 0.5, which is why 1,000 cuts gives about 17 million. The reel is 73 s, six rounds (10, 50, 100, 250, 500, 1,000 cuts), one locked camera, knife sounds only and no music; it got about 1.5 million likes on a 62k-follower account. The node page has the build steps, the round timings and four knife sounds cut into our library.

items.title: Propeller-gun interrupter gear: the render quality bar for our Blender explainers
items.creator: @touchmediapoint0
items.teaches: A 22 s mechanism explainer: a fighter plane turns to glass, and the gears, cam and rods that time the gun to fire between the propeller blades light up one by one as the voice names them. It looks premium because of worn, bevelled metal with real reflections, a glass body, a blurred sky over a glossy floor, very shallow focus on close-ups, and colour as state (orange = working, green = safe gap, blue = trigger). Our Blender pipeline already has the textures, motion blur and camera rules; it lacks real reflections (Cycles or light probes), bevels on every part, wear and grime, glowing state colours and any compositing (bloom, grain). The entry lists the steps to close that gap, starting with a 20-frame look test rendered three ways.

items.title: Remove the AI look from coded motion graphics: a curve per move, uneven offsets, living holds
items.creator: @hugh_candoit
items.teaches: Yes, useful: the post shows why Claude-made motion graphics all move the same, and the cause is real in our own installed HyperFrames skill (one 0.6 s ease-out default on every move, every item entering from 24 px below, 0.08 s apart). The fix is how an After Effects animator keys: a curve chosen per move (land, heavy, whip), duration from distance and weight, exits faster than entrances, one lead element with the rest reacting at uneven offsets, most text simply cutting on, and holds that keep drifting. We wrote our own version with values. The creator's skill is comment-gated and was not obtained.
items.use: Example: every HyperFrames title, map, lineage tree or stat card for KaalAurKatha reels follows these six rules instead of the skill's defaults; also website and app UI motion.

items.title: Verbicon: one letter becomes what the word means
items.creator: @logomaker.vn
items.teaches: Five wordmarks where one letter turns into what the word means: the G of GUN is a pistol, both A's of SANDALS are flip-flops, the i of Rain is a cloud with rain falling, the o of slow is a snail shell. The word stays in a plain font and only one letter changes, at the same weight, so it still reads at a glance. For us: a cover or title-card word where one Hindi letter or matra becomes the story's object (the ring in मुद्रिका, the mace in गदा), animated as a letter morph for title stings.
items.use: Example: the cover title of the next KaalAurKatha video with the ring drawn into मुद्रिका, or a chapter-card sting where the ा of गदा morphs into a mace on the beat.

items.title: Monster-mouth boot render breakdown: how realistic 3D renders are built, layer by layer (Blender recipe)
items.creator: @anklovee
items.teaches: A 20 s render breakdown that adds one layer at a time: clay model, then a key and a rim light, a fake fog, materials, a spotlight for each detail (15+ lights), sculpted teeth, a hangar environment with glowing screens, depth of field, smoke, then grade, bloom and grain. The creator used Cinema 4D, Octane, Substance Painter and ZBrush (3 to 10 minutes a frame on a top GPU); every step has a free Blender match (Cycles, sculpt mode, shape keys, light linking, a free hangar HDRI, Blender smoke). Realism comes mostly from lighting each detail on its own and from giving glass and chrome something to reflect, not from the model. The shelf entry turns it into a 9-step recipe for any hero shot.

items.title: Seven UI-motion sound effects (ripple, warp, bass crack, cyber shift, glitch, cine strike), all extracted
items.creator: @adrianrazen
items.teaches: A sound-pack demo for UI and SaaS animations: seven named sounds, each played alone on silence, plus two unnamed ones on the end card. All nine were cut into our sound library as clean WAV files, named by what they sound like (ripple flutters, an alien warp, a bass crack, a cyber shift, a heavy distortion glitch, a cinematic strike, a double-stutter text reveal, a glow hum). They are loud, so start them 10 to 12 dB down. The full pack is comment-gated and was not obtained.

items.title: Texturize: emboss a paper texture into tape, text and background (EffectCraft, tested)
items.creator: @con.tendo
items.teaches: After Effects' Texturize effect reads a hidden paper scan and lights it like a relief on any layer, so a flat tape strip, a word or a background picks up real paper creases. Steps: get a free paper texture (Texturelabs), put it in the comp with its eye off, add Stylize > Texturize to each element, pick the paper as Texture Layer, set Light Direction about 33 degrees and Contrast about 2. The tip is to texture every layer separately (background, text, strokes). EffectCraft has the same effect and our test render works; an SVG version for HyperFrames works too.
items.use: Example: KaalAurKatha chapter and verse cards, maps and lineage trees on aged paper or palm-leaf texture, torn-tape name tags in a character intro, collage hooks for ads.

items.title: Finishing checklist: one clip built in seven passes (raw, grade, hook text, overlays, graphics, zoom, SFX and music)
items.creator: @motionart.vfx
items.teaches: An editor replays the same 3-second talking-head clip seven times, adding one layer per pass with a white flash between: raw, colour grade, text hook, styled text overlays, graphics and effects, punch-in zooms, then sound effects and music. Only the last pass looks finished. We turned it into a finishing checklist that maps every pass onto our apps and the techniques already in the library, plus a final 'which layer is missing' check. Open question for you on the dashboard: should every edit carry every layer, or only some formats?
items.use: Example: run the checklist on every KaalAurKatha video, client ad and fitness reel before export; or copy the seven-pass format as a 'how this edit was built' reel.

items.creator: @diego.a.does
items.teaches: Two colours do 90% of a website's work and one unexpected accent gets the last 10%, used only on the button you want pressed. items.title: OTP code screen motion: digits rise in, a checking wave, collapse into a checkmark, SMS autofill
items.creator: @charles.unemployed
items.teaches: An AI-made purple verification-code screen is cleaned in five passes: no gradients, auto-submit on the 6th digit, fewer words, borderless white tiles on an iridescent off-white card. Then every state gets motion: each digit rises in over about 100 ms, a left-to-right dim wave means 'checking', the six tiles collapse to a dot that draws a checkmark with 'Verified', and a code from an SMS fills all six digits in about 300 ms. The node page records the layout, sampled hex colours, fonts and a 30 fps timing table, enough to rebuild it on the web or in a React Native app. It is queued in the UI animation library to build.
items.use: Example: the phone-number sign-in step of our next app (Pocket Ledger first), re-skinned to its palette; the same enter, checking, success pattern also fits a payment confirm or a sync.

items.creator: @zaylento

items.creator: @riddleordie

It opens on a 5-4-3-2-1 countdown and "caught, sent back, again", pins three numbered rules as cards that never leave the screen, starts a live GUARD 05:00 timer, knocks out run, hide and wait for night, then "pause and think", "write your answer in the comments" and "follow, the next escape is harder". items.title: Log to cinematic in one node: the greenery grade (settings read off the panel)
items.creator: @tonelab.io
items.teaches: One Resolve node (the paid ToneLab Chroma plug-in) takes a DJI drone log shot of a green ridge to a deep green, gold-lit grade. Every value was read off the panel: camera DJI D-Log (Mavic 3), look Ethereal Green 5 at 120, basic adjustments (Exposure 1.381, Lift -4.8, Gamma -21.4, Gain -23.8, Highlights -99.1, Temperature -6.7, Tint -2.0, Saturation 0.821, Contrast 1.917, Fade 24.4), finishing tone Rich Gold Glow at 90. We rebuilt it without the plug-in (D-Log LUT, curve, colour balance, saturation 1.3) and it matched the reel within 0.03 on every colour band.

items.creator: @tonelab.io

Reel values: DJI D-Log (Mavic 4/Zenmuse X9), look Cinema Warm 7 at 100, split tone Teal & Orange at 71.4. FilmCraft already has built-in input LUTs for Sony, Panasonic, Canon, ARRI, Apple and DJI log, so no plug-in is needed. Your request to generate a log-style AI clip is written up as a prompt method and a proposed rule (flat ungraded wording, what to avoid, a measured check on arrival, then a grade-back); nothing was generated.

items.title: Two-effect duck: music under narration (−20…−30 dB, wide dip at 2.2 kHz, Lowpass 2.5 kHz)
items.creator: @artzenmedia
items.teaches: Two effects on the music, not the voice, so narration sits in front. First the music level comes down 20 to 30 dB depending on the song. Then Mastering with the Make Room For Vocals preset (a wide -11.5 dB dip at 2168.5 Hz, Q 0.3, with a stereo widen) and a Lowpass at 2500 Hz (stay between 2 and 3 kHz; 400 to 550 Hz sounds underwater). In FilmCraft one Parametric Equalizer does the dip and the lowpass with exact values, keyframed to the voice regions so the music opens up again between lines.
items.use: Example: every narration-bed score in a KaalAurKatha video (e.g. the ritual cue under the narrator), keyed to the narration and dub tracks; never on a sung or beat-built cue.

Six are new and NOT installed: jakubkrehel/skills (Better Typography plus colour, layout and review skills), Hallmark (themes plus a browser linter), hue (brand to design system), interface-design (design memory plugin), the shadcn/ui skill and Google Stitch's Extract DESIGN.md. items.title: Tangerine: convert or compress any file on the Mac with Shift-drag
items.creator: @metav3rse
items.teaches: Tangerine is a Mac App Store app. Shift-drag any file and a wheel of formats opens (images, audio, video, PDF, subtitles, archives); Shift+Option-drag opens tools: compress, crop, strip metadata, add a background, redact, split a PDF, trim a video. Everything runs offline on the Mac, and the result lands next to the original. It needs Apple silicon and macOS 13+, so our MacBook fits. It is free for 20 actions, then a one-time unlock (reports say €17 to €35, so check the price in ₹). It is not open source and has no Windows version. We can already do all of this with ffmpeg and ImageMagick through Claude; Tangerine just makes the one-off jobs instant.
items.use: Example: Shift-drag a WebP reference image to PNG before uploading it to ChatGPT, or strip a photo's metadata before sending it. Batch exports stay with Claude + ffmpeg.

items.title: YouTube Shows: turn saga playlists into seasons and episodes
items.creator: @Romayroh
items.teaches: The 'setting' is real. In YouTube Studio go to Content, then Playlists, then Options, then Add show features, and a playlist becomes a TV-style Show with seasons, episodes and artwork. YouTube's Help page confirms the steps, the serial vs non-serial order, Shorts series, and that shows may appear under Recommended shows and Continue watching. The video's bigger claims are NOT confirmed by YouTube: views doubling, higher RPM from TV, the show 'teaching the algorithm', the recommendation feed being hidden. For us: make each saga (Janasthana, Raktabeej) a serial show with a 16:9 banner and backdrop, pin it on the Home tab, and measure the result for 28 days before trusting it.
items.use: Example: convert the Raktabeej playlist into a serial show, add the show artwork at the post-production stage, and add each new episode to its season at upload.

items.title: Same assets, four layouts: a design practice drill
items.creator: @designs_by_max
items.teaches: Gather 4-5 asset types for one subject (hero image, title, body text, a small icon or map), make one version in your own style, then make at least four different layouts with exactly the same assets. Changing only the layout trains you to always have several options and is a fair way to compare them.
items.use: Shared without a note. Example: when showing design options for a cover, poster or hero section, keep one asset set and vary only the layout four times, each with a name.

items.title: Pull-to-reveal packaging: sleeve, tray and revolving wrap, with a dieline to build one
items.creator: @akanksha.sureka
items.teaches: The box is a tray sliding in an open sleeve, plus a paper loop glued to the tray's rear edge that wraps round the sleeve's top panel (about twice the sleeve length). Pulling the tray scrolls the loop, so the printed top changes from artwork A to artwork B; the tall and triangular bottle versions are the same loop turned vertical, with die-cut windows. The entry explains board weights, how a printer die-cuts, creases, window-patches and glues it, and we made a parametric dieline script plus a ready template to build one from card. The mechanism matches a US patent family, so build it to learn, but check before producing it commercially.
items.use: Can you learn the mechanism of how this physical packaging can be made? Example: a launch or influencer kit for a client product where pulling the tray reveals the campaign line, or a saree gift box whose top changes to a festival greeting.

items.title: Couldn't fetch: login-gated reel (animation presets)
items.teaches: Couldn't download it. Two tries got Instagram's "empty media response" (the post needs a login), and the public embed page says "The link to this photo or video may be broken, or the post may have been removed", with no caption or creator. Nothing was learned and no login was tried. If you want it, screen-record the reel on your Pixel and share the recording, or tell me which animation presets it shows.

items.title: The Red Hat of AI inference: a business around free open models
items.creator: @anshmehra.in
items.teaches: Red Hat got rich selling trust (support, security, certification) around free Linux, and the same gap exists now around free open AI models like Llama, DeepSeek and Gemma. For a solo engineer the realistic businesses are: (A) audit and move companies from expensive AI APIs to open models, (B) a private AI box for small firms that cannot send their data abroad, (C) later, an open-model creative pipeline for creators. Build first: a small 'AI bill cutter' web app that runs a company's real prompts on open models and shows the quality and the monthly rupee saving. Push only if 10 audit requests (or 3 paid audits) come in within 30 days.
items.use: Example: build the AI bill cutter MVP with his web skills, use the studio's own move to local open models (Whisper) as the first case study, and run the choice through Roast Room.

items.title: Personality in a website: a rugged-and-bold racing brand, brief to final site
items.creator: @ayzz.thedesigner
items.teaches: A music-only reel, read from the frames. The client's email says "Rugged & Bold". He sketches two hero layouts on paper (heading, subject, social proof, CTA), maps Rugged to stone textures and Bold to black + red, makes a moodboard, a sitemap and a fonts sheet, then builds a red hero split around the bike, a gear grid where hovering reveals a rider, and athlete cards. As you asked, this designer now has his own brain section: his process, rules, critique checklist, references and colour themes. A lens menu now scores him against the other design creators per use case, for you to pick from at the start of every design phase.
items.use: Example: the next client brand site opens with the lens table, where this designer scores 10.

items.title: Landing page redesign: every mistake in the before, and the fix
items.creator: @ayzz.thedesigner
items.teaches: 15 before-and-after fixes on an ads-agency landing page. A cluttered hero with no focal point (he calls it the biggest mistake in AI-made designs) and a vague slogan become one focal visual that tells the business, plus a headline that states the offer. Social proof moves into or right after the hero and reads as an average, not a one-off. The brand-name explainer and the written promise are cut. A problem section with a visual, case studies, a 4-step process, testimonials and a footer CTA are added, all in one brand style. Honest answer to your question: an AI-default build would come out close to the before, so these fixes are now a 10-question checklist run on every draft.
items.use: Example: run the critique checklist on the Pocket Ledger marketing page or any kaalaurkatha.com landing page before showing it.

items.title: His 7 design inspiration resources (full YouTube video analysed)
items.creator: @ayzz.thedesigner
items.teaches: The reel teases a YouTube video, "Design award winning websites using these resources" (8:52), which was found and read in full from its captions. Seven sources, each matched to a job: MaxiBestOf (by industry, by font, by section), Muzli (a daily feed), Pinterest (non-web ideas), Awwwards (the ceiling), Supahero (heroes), Recent Design (motion and 3D) and Dark Mode Design (dark sites). MaxiBestOf, Muzli and the GoFullPage screenshot extension are new to the brain. His method: combine pieces of ~10 references rather than copying one, make 6-7 hero variations, and keep the references beside the frame you're designing.
items.use: Example: on the next kaalaurkatha.com page, recommend Dark Mode Design (a dark site) + Supahero (hero) + MaxiBestOf font search before designing.

items.title: Hallmark: anti-AI-slop design skill for websites and apps
items.creator: @thevarunmayya
items.teaches: Hallmark (github.com/Nutlope/hallmark, MIT, by Together AI) is a Claude Code skill and plugin that builds pages from 3 of 50 named themes, then opens them in a real browser at 8 widths and fixes the 'AI-made' tells before you ship. It can also redesign or audit an existing site, and it checks that no link, form field or handler went missing in a redesign. We already have similar taste skills (Impeccable, Taste), but not the browser lint or the redesign safety check. Nothing is installed yet: Keep means read all its code, install it hidden, and make it our design skill for websites and apps only.
items.use: Example: redesign a kaalaurkatha.com page or a Pocket Ledger screen with /hallmark redesign, showing 3 named theme previews first, and never use it for covers, thumbnails or ad creatives.

items.title: 60-30-10 colour rule on a product ad (repost, second source)
items.creator: @designs_by_max
items.teaches: Give every colour one job: 60% background, 30% the text and content on top, 10% the brand colour only on the button and one phrase of the headline. This is a repost of a 60-30-10 reel already in the library, so it was filed as a second source with its new demo (a skincare ad going from a flat grey version to slate, white and a pink accent).
items.use: Design rule for using colors in design. Example: on a product image ad, put the brand colour only on the Order Now button and one headline phrase; on a website, only on the main button and one highlighted word.

items.title: Opium stretch effect: horizontal smear + grainy B&W flash on beat cuts
items.creator: @jackwhoedits
items.teaches: "OPM" reads as OPIUM: every card says "Opium Stretch Effect" (the reel never says OPM; please confirm). On a beat cut, a 13-frame Stretch transition centred on the cut smears the shot sideways (Bell curve, Ease In 0, Ease Out 33, Dissolve 25%, Angle 90, Stretch 100%), under a ~10-frame adjustment layer with Noise + keyframed Extract that turns the flash into grainy, near-binary black and white. The Noise/Extract values are inside a comment-gated preset, so our FilmCraft rebuild proposes them; FilmCraft's own Stretch is the classic one, so the smear is rebuilt with Directional Blur + Scale Width. 3 s preview saved.
items.use: Example: in a short or teaser of the current mythological series, put one Opium stretch on each beat cut where a drop of the demon's blood becomes a new clone, so the multiplication hits as a hard black-and-white rhythm.

items.title: Brand first, then the website: questionnaire to live CRM tracking
items.creator: @ayzz.thedesigner
items.teaches: Branding a client before building the site: a short questionnaire (what you do, who you sell to, 3-5 admired brands, the feeling a visitor should have (pick 3), the brand as a person walking into a meeting in 3-5 words). Then logo sketches on paper, the client's existing colours enhanced, brand guidelines, a sitemap, and straight to design because the branding already set the personality. The homepage has a 3D hero showing everything the business does, plus social proof and one CTA. Then pages per division, a catalogue, shipment tracking fed from their CRM, and a responsive Webflow build.
items.use: Example: for the next client who needs a brand and a site, send his questionnaire as a doc before the first call, then follow steps 1-3 of the designer page.

items.title: Agency website redesign, the whole process from audit to Webflow
items.creator: @ayzz.thedesigner
items.teaches: A redesign done in order: audit the old site's problems, find where customers come from (referrals, so the site is the conversion point), sitemap, a two-part moodboard (styles to pick + the client's own references), then a hero and one signature brand element (hand-drawn strokes) that runs through every section and interaction. Sections go hero → problem → projects → services → testimonials → a chat-style FAQ, then a Webflow build with performance and responsive passes. It is now the step-by-step process on this designer's own brain page. Scraping his whole profile is logged as a follow-up waiting for your go.
items.use: Example: the next kaalaurkatha.com pass or a client site follows the 12 steps on his designer page, built in Astro + GSAP instead of Webflow.

items.title: Five fruit colour palettes for landing pages, by use case
items.creator: @ayzz.thedesigner
items.teaches: Five palettes taken from fruit (strawberry, grape, lemon, passion fruit, peach), each with 4 named swatches and a landing page built in it: motorsport, a premium product, a fashion drop, personal care, food delivery. Each one is used as ground + display type + light neutral, with the fourth colour as the accent (60-30-10). The hex codes were sampled from the frames.

items.title: Motion tracking: text label pinned to a fingertip via a tracked null
items.creator: @_joshhoffman
items.teaches: Point tracking in After Effects (EffectCraft for us): Track Motion, put the box on a high-contrast spot (he drew a dot on his finger), set Options to Stop Tracking so it halts when it loses the point, analyse forward, then re-seat the box and continue. Apply the track to a Null object, parent a text layer to the null, and turn on motion blur so the text sits in the shot. It's the same tracking as an earlier reel, so it was added as a second source on that page, which now has a preview.
items.use: No note from him (untitled row). Example: a title or label that rides an object in frame, like the name of a divine weapon pinned to the weapon in a mythology short, or a callout that follows a product or a lift in a fitness reel.

items.title: Dynamic Link round-trip (Premiere ↔ After Effects) and our FilmCraft ↔ EffectCraft equivalent
items.creator: @varculin
items.teaches: Premiere's Dynamic Link: cut the part that needs effects, right-click → Replace With After Effects Composition, build the effect in AE, and the Premiere timeline updates by itself. Your question: FilmCraft and EffectCraft have NO live link, but every piece of a near-equivalent exists: render the EffectCraft comp to one fixed file, place it on V2 in FilmCraft, and after each change re-render and run Refresh Changed Media. Claude can do that as one command per change. Not tested yet.

items.title: Three movie-clip search sites: ClipCafe, PlayPhrase.me, Yarn
items.creator: @myselfakshayy
items.teaches: Three sites for finding a film moment fast: ClipCafe (search a film, get its scenes with dialogue), PlayPhrase.me (type a line, hear every film that says it) and Yarn (quote search with download). Good for finding a reference shot or a reaction insert. They are studio films, so 'free download' is not a licence: on YouTube a clip can get a Content ID claim, so clear it before anything is published.
items.use: Finding a reference scene when a script beat says 'like the scene in \<film>', or a meme/reaction line for a short draft (search the line on PlayPhrase.me first). Not as footage in a published video without clearing it.

items.title: Tire 'hairs' explainer: follow one material through the machine (quality bar #2)
items.creator: @speedy_devv
items.teaches: A 55 s 3D explainer of why new tires have hairs (rubber squeezed into the mold's 1 mm air vents). What makes it good: it follows one patch of rubber through the press on a scale ladder (tire, tread, vent, bubble), puts one small-caps leader-line label on each spoken word, shows every number as an object (350 vs 35 PSI gauges, a 0 to 100 mile counter), and adds tiny honesty tags like 'Magnified illustration'. Filed as the second quality-bar reference for the Blender channel, with a Blender build plan; its mascot host is optional and its figures need checking before reuse.
items.use: Example: before the next cutaway episode's script locks, check it against both quality-bar entries (scale ladder, leader-line labels, honesty tags, numbers as objects, loop ending).

items.title: Surreal building slide (tracked mask + CC RepeTile)
items.creator: @justinserran
items.teaches: One tower slides upward out of the skyline while the rest of the shot stays still, and it never runs out because it is tiled above and below itself. Steps: mask and track the tower, duplicate the layer and invert the top mask, pre-compose the bottom copy and crop it to the mask (120x940), scale it to fill the gap, add CC RepeTile (Expand Up/Down 500), then keyframe Position upward. No plugins. A 4.5 s preview is saved with the node.
items.use: Example: a temple shikhara or palace wall sliding up as a 'realm shifts' beat in a KaalAurKatha edit.

items.title: 20 named lighting setups, picked by the mood of the photo
items.creator: @ai.volve.news
items.teaches: One portrait relit 20 ways (dappled, high key, low key, golden hour, moonlight, venetian blinds, candlelight, gels, clamshell, rim light, silhouette, lightning and more) shows that the light alone sets the mood. The creator's prompts were comment-gated, so we wrote our own prompt phrase for each setup plus a mood → light table.

items.title: Perfume-brand site: lit stone niches, tap a bottle to zoom into its room
items.creator: @ascenta.studio
items.teaches: A luxury product site built as a dark stone wall with five lit niches, one bottle per niche. Hover brightens a niche's spotlight; tap zooms the camera into that niche, with the bottle on the right and the name, notes and price on the left. On mobile the wall becomes a 2-column grid. It suits any showpiece product (perfume, watches, jewellery, a hero saree); the trick is one niche plate and one light rig reused for every product, with only the light colour changing.
items.use: Example: a client pitch for a perfume or jewellery brand, or single hero sarees for a saree shop, built with GSAP Flip over PhotoCraft cut-outs.

items.title: 8-beat short-form script structure: hook, lead, 3 value blocks split by 2 open loops, CTA
items.creator: @realskytan
items.teaches: A script skeleton for reels and shorts in 8 beats: Hook, Lead (holds viewers to the 10-second mark), Body 1 (pay off the hook early), an open loop, Body 2, a second open loop, Body 3, CTA. An open loop is the last line of a block that leaves something unresolved ("but that's not the craziest part…"), and it re-hooks the viewer mid-video. The CTA turns the warmest viewers into the next step; his is a comment-keyword lead magnet, which we recorded but didn't act on. Filed on a new shelf, youtube_story/script_structure, with notes on how it maps to our reels and where the Daksh long-form rules apply instead.
items.use: Shared without a note, so it is proposed as Only when asked by name. Example from your work: at the script stage of the next KaalAurKatha reel, label each line Hook / Lead / B1 / L1 / B2 / L2 / B3 / CTA, make sure Body 1 lands before ~10 s, and end each story block on a Hindi loop line ("lekin asli kahani to abhi baaki thi…").

items.title: Neon Glow look: Find Edges (Invert) + Tint to cyan + VR Glow
items.creator: @cinemawithmayank
items.teaches: Turns any shot into glowing neon line art with three stock Premiere effects: Find Edges (Invert ticked, Blend 0 %) gives white edges on black, Tint maps white to cyan, and VR Glow (Luma Threshold 0.10, Radius 99 to 185, Brightness about 1.4–1.5, Saturation 1.0) makes the lines bloom. The values were read from close-up crops of the panel because the Hindi voice-over didn't transcribe. A 3.5 s preview is saved with the node.
items.use: No note (untitled row), so proposed as "only when asked by name". Example: reveal Ayodhya's or Lanka's palace as a glowing gold or cyan line drawing on a title card before it fills in with colour; it works best on architecture, not faces.

Do the same in an edit: pick a theme and build an SFX set, for example a paper scrunch on every text animation in and a paper slide on every text out, and reuse it on every similar animation. No sounds were extracted: Mario's are Nintendo's and the paper ones play under music.

items.title: Thermal Grunge: a 1 s thermal-camera stinger (heat-map LUT, Posterize Time 8, halftone + paper textures)
items.creator: @studioznaak
items.teaches: Between two normal shots, cut to a punch-in close-up for about one second and make it look like a thermal camera: a heat-map LUT in Lumetri, then Exposure 1.5, Contrast -150, Highlights 90, Shadows 25, Posterize Time 8 fps, a halftone texture on Overlay and a paper texture on Screen, all nested. A whoosh, shutter and camera-flash SFX sell the hit. Their LUT and textures are comment-gated, so ours uses our own false-colour LUT. A 3 s preview is saved next to the node.

items.title: Flash Whip: 2-frame white silhouette of the next subject, then a whip from below

items.title: Five ways to add texture to video: grain, paper, dust, light leaks, texture in text (blend mode + opacity)

For our AI shots, every shot in the list gets a first-frame and last-frame focus position, written in absolute terms in each prompt.

The reel's example is Nolan recording his own ticking watch, with Hans Zimmer building the whole Dunkirk score on it. You never notice it, but you feel your pulse rise. A mài can be a sound, a visual motif or a question the viewer chases.

items.title: Hit, bounce back, fall: three stacked Transforms with motion blur
items.creator: @adityaxsoon
items.teaches: A thrown object (a pixel potion in the demo) flies in, hits the subject, bounces back a little and drops. Nest the sprite and stack three Transform effects (hit 2192 to 960 px, then bounce back, then fall), each with Shutter Angle 180, not 360. Start each move's keyframes inside the previous move so it reads as one continuous motion with no robotic pause.
items.use: No note (untitled share). Example: a comic beat in a KaalAurKatha short where an object is thrown at a character, or a product in a client ad dropping into frame with a believable recoil.

items.title: Gestalt layout: proximity, alignment, then scale, detail, contrast
items.creator: @aevyvideoschool
items.teaches: A layout's job is to guide attention, not just to fit things wherever there is space. Use Gestalt principles: proximity (keep related items together) and alignment/continuity (one line for the eye to travel). If the design doesn't stand out, exaggerate scale. If it looks plain, add relevant detail. If it has no focal point, add contrast.
items.use: Example: run every thumbnail, cover and ad creative through proximity, then alignment, then scale, detail and contrast before calling it done.

items.title: Startup blueprint: problem, ICP, TAM/SAM/SOM, MVP, pivot
items.creator: @buildwithreema
items.teaches: Six gates for a startup idea. 1) Start from a real pain point, not a solution looking for a problem. 2) Pick the ideal customer profile (ICP): the people who have that pain and will pay. 3) Size the market with TAM/SAM/SOM. 4) Build in public. 5) Ship the MVP and ask users if they like it: no means pivot at once, yes means keep showing up. 6) Raise money only if speed matters.
items.use: No note (untitled share). Example: when you bring up a business idea, check it against these six gates next to Roast Room.

items.creator: @theeditingcanvas

items.title: Profile bounce: a screenshot splits into layers that bounce in one by one
items.creator: @octagonediting
items.teaches: Cut a screenshot (an Instagram profile) into about 14 layers, one per element, using rectangle masks. Key out the black background with Color Key, then keyframe each layer flying into place over about 20 frames. An inertial-bounce expression (freq 3, decay 5) adds the overshoot, and the layers are staggered 5 frames apart. The creator's Split Mask script is gated, so the node rebuilds that step by hand.
items.use: No note given. Example: a KaalAurKatha character card whose name, weapon and boons assemble line by line, or a client app screen that builds itself in a promo.

items.title: Six cuts: repeat, match, invisible, smash, L and J
items.creator: @planetinpixel
items.teaches: Six named cuts: repeat (show an action twice to stress it), match (same action carries across two scenes), invisible (hide the cut in motion), smash (cut between very different moods), L (scene 1's audio runs over scene 2, good for flashbacks) and J (scene 2's audio starts early). From now on every edit plan names the cut between each pair of shots.

items.title: Colour theory for realism: analogous palette + one complementary accent + blue shadows
items.creator: @pixeleditorshub
items.teaches: Films keep a scene's colours close together on the colour wheel to push one emotion (red = danger, orange = heat or anger, blue = isolation or fear). To make a hero stand out they add ONE colour from the opposite side (a teal light behind warm skin, a green dress, a blue shirt). Shadows, smoke and fog are tinted blue, never pure black. Filed with a prompt recipe (palette + accent + shadow colour) and a vectorscope grading routine for AI clips.

A mirror (band) mask on the landscape layer starts as a thin line at the chin and is rotated to about -22° and widened, so the backgrounds strobe in behind a still subject. items.title: Floating clones: make yourself levitate (roto + keyframes)
items.creator: @futurist__
items.teaches: Shoot a low wide hero shot, then shoot yourself jumping from the same spot at a high frame rate. Roto each jump out (Roto Brush in After Effects = EffectCraft), shrink it, place it in the sky and keyframe it up a little so it drifts. Repeat for 6-8 copies, then roto the hero out too and put that layer on top so the clones float behind him.

items.title: The Speed effect: cut-out zips out of frame in 6 frames
items.creator: @futurist__
items.teaches: Film a fast move, then the same framing empty. Cut the move clip at take-off and keep just 6 frames over the empty plate. Roto Brush the person out, keyframe Position from rest to fully off-frame to the left, and turn on Motion Blur, so they streak out and leave the location behind. Repeat for every clip. This needs a static camera.

items.title: Ink transition: ink overlay as a reversed Luma Track Matte
items.creator: @azeems.feed
items.teaches: Clip A on track 1, clip B on track 2, a free black-on-white ink overlay on track 3. Put Track Matte Key on clip B: Matte = Video 3, Composite Using = Matte Luma, Reverse ON. B then bleeds in through the growing ink blots, and captions on a higher track stay untouched. No plug-in, nothing gatekept.
items.use: Example: a KaalAurKatha short cutting from a palace to a battlefield under word-pop captions, with the ink reading as a manuscript page. We can draw our own ink blots in EffectCraft so we never depend on a downloaded overlay.

items.title: Cosmic chrome text: 5-colour palette mapped through a bevel depth, Phase animated, Deep Glow on top (paid plug-in settings)
items.creator: @graphic_stuzo
items.teaches: A glowing chrome script word. The reel is a settings list for the paid After Effects plug-in 'Cosmic' (palette of 5 colours, angle 11, offset -100, saturation 132, brightness 130; depth angle 115, contrast 250, bulge 135, rounding 78; its own glow off; animate Phase) plus Deep Glow 2 (threshold 74, smooth 35, saturation bias 20). We do not have either plug-in, so the node carries a native rebuild: Bevel Alpha for the depth, Colorama for the 5-colour cycle with Phase keyframed, native Glow. The download was only 360p.
items.use: An episode title or deity name in chrome with a gold-crimson-indigo palette where the light travels along the strokes; brand words in brand colours for client reels. Sibling of the shimmer-text node from the same run; pick by whether the shimmer should swirl or travel.

items.title: Colour grade system: one accent colour, one scheme, mute everything else (luminance then saturation)
items.creator: @aevyvideoschool
items.teaches: Stop fixing colours one slider at a time. Pick ONE accent colour (he eyedrops the lantern orange), choose a scheme for the rest (complementary, monochromatic or analogous), pull the other colours into that palette, and in the HSL mixer drop the luminance and then the saturation of every hue the scene does not need. The neon izakaya demo goes from five fighting colours to orange-on-teal. Filed as a four-line grading checklist.
items.use: A checklist before any Lumetri/Resolve grade and for muting stray greens and magentas in generated plates instead of regenerating them; also the way to phrase palettes in image prompts (one accent, teal shadows, muted greens).

items.title: Prism Lens transition: 12+2-frame nested window into a two-slot transition comp with a prism/light-leak smear
items.creator: @ulucfx
items.teaches: The structure of a sold Premiere transition pack: razor the last 12 frames of clip A and the first 2 of clip B, nest each, drop the transition on top and drag the nests into Media Holder 01/02. Five looks: light leak, horizontal and vertical stretch smears, soft zoom, RGB prism split. The preset itself is gatekept (comment 'prism' for a DM), so the node records the 14-frame structure and a native smear we build ourselves in EffectCraft.

items.title: Shutter Slide: 10-frame photo stack, each photo drops in from above with Transform shutter blur
items.creator: @theeditingcanvas
items.teaches: A photo-burst slam after a video shot. Set every photo to 10 frames, stagger them stair-step on rising tracks 3-4 frames apart, put the Transform effect on the first one with Position keyframed from y=-660 (above frame) to its resting place over 4 frames and Shutter Angle 180 for the motion blur, then Paste Attributes onto the rest. No plug-in. Values read from the Premiere panel because the Hindi VO did not transcribe.
items.use: A beat-synced burst of 6-8 iconography stills before the hook line of a KaalAurKatha facts reel, a product colourway burst in a client ad before the price card, or a PR montage on the fitness page.

items.title: Gradient shimmer text: blurred colour map through the type with CC Blobbylize, threshold + cross-blur sheen, glow
items.creator: @cancelled.name
items.teaches: A chrome-like title where a moving colour gradient lives inside the letters. Any colourful image is blurred and swirled with Turbulent Displace, pushed through the text's alpha with CC Blobbylize (softness 4, cut away 25), then a duplicate gets CC Threshold 63.8% + CC Cross Blur 300/300 in Screen for the sheen, and a glow on top. Every effect is native After Effects except Deep Glow, which our native Glow replaces. Full values are in the node.
items.use: Hero titles: a KaalAurKatha episode title or deity name in Devanagari with a gold/saffron colour map instead of magenta; a brand word in a client reel with the fabric photo as the bump map. Not for captions or lower thirds.

items.title: End any song smoothly: 10-frame nest + Studio Reverb at max decay (FilmCraft / SoundCraft)
items.creator: @himanshujainfilms
items.teaches: How to stop the music where the cut needs it without an ugly cut or dissolve. Cut the last 10 frames of the song into their own clip, nest it, put a ~5 s Black Video inside the nest so the clip can be extended past the music, Constant Power crossfades on both sides, then Studio Reverb on that nested clip with Decay dragged from 2500 to 10000 ms (everything else default: dry 75 / wet 25). The last note rings out over the silence. Sibling of the music-start reel filed earlier today.
items.use: Every short where the music must end before the last line or the end card: KaalAurKatha shorts, the Raktabeej teaser's final title card, a client ad before the logo sting. Headless ffmpeg stand-in is written in the node; SoundCraft reverb pass to verify in Phase 2.

items.title: The 60-30-10 colour rule: give every colour one job
items.creator: @designs_by_max
items.teaches: Don't let every colour do everything: 60% of the design is the background colour, 30% a contrasting colour for the content on top, and the brand/accent colour is only 10%, on the important parts (main text, button). The demo rebuilds a Japanese market poster from all-brown to charcoal 60 / white type 30 / brand brown 10 on one headline word, and it reads at a glance. Same split as good cinematography.
items.use: kaalaurkatha.com and any UI: dark ground 60, text and cards 30, saffron/gold accent 10 on CTAs and one headline word. Client image ads and KaalAurKatha covers: the brand colour is the 10%, never the 60%. Pairs with the text-size ratio rule filed yesterday.

items.title: Piyush Pandey's rules for Meta ads: problem first, local tongue, inhale life
items.creator: @adsandcopy
items.teaches: Three of Piyush Pandey's principles applied to Meta ads: (1) open on the exact consumer problem and close on proof of the product as the solution, with the actor, accent and location matching the audience; (2) write in the buyer's regional language (his proof: 150 ads for Supernova AI in Malayalam, Kannada, Telugu, Hindi, Gujarati); (3) 'inhale life': ideas come from observing how people actually talk, so write copy raw and authentic and think twice before letting AI write it. Three more principles are in his next reel (list blurred, not read).
items.use: A three-line check on every a client ad brief: first 2 s = the customer's complaint in her words; the ad's language = the buyer's language; last shot = the product doing the thing. Shapes the brief only; the VO still comes from her Notion Script Doc.

items.title: Visual exaggeration conceptual ads: blow the one benefit up until it is impossible
items.creator: @deepaksisodiadesigns
items.teaches: A concepting method for image ads: pick the product's single benefit and show it exaggerated to an impossible degree; the bigger the exaggeration the harder it lands. Four examples read from the frames: Otrivin (nostrils bricked up, 'Break the block'), Lay's (surfer on a wave of crisps), Michelin (a tyre in a ring box, 'Man's most precious gift') and his own Skybags ad (suitcase lifted by balloons, 'Too light to stay grounded'). Reference pool: Pinterest search 'Visual Exaggeration Conceptual Ads'.
items.use: A brief rule for a client / a client image ads: which one benefit, and what is the impossible version of it? Also the prompt shape for AI image ads ([hero object] [impossible exaggeration of one benefit], flat background, brand colour, copy space). Stored as a method; nothing generated.

items.title: Radial shutter transition: edge-only directional blur + 2-frame flash (FilmCraft)
items.creator: @genovix.in
items.teaches: A cut that stutters through a few 3-frame slivers, with the frame edges smeared by a vertical Directional Blur (angle 90) on an adjustment layer while the subject stays sharp through an inverted ellipse mask on Opacity (feather 200, expansion 100; Alpha Adjust with Ignore Alpha on). A second 2-frame adjustment layer in Linear Dodge (Add) sits at the head of every sliver as the flash. No plug-in. Not shown: the blur length.
items.use: Hard location cuts that need a hit in short-form: the Raktabeej teaser palace-to-battlefield cut, KaalAurKatha shorts, the product-reveal cut in a client ad. Phase 2 can rebuild it in FilmCraft and verify frame by frame against the reel's own demo (0\:00-0\:03).

items.title: 16 marketing psychology levers, Level 1–4, with Indian examples (scarcity to bandwagon)
items.creator: @dhruv_wan
items.teaches: A hand-held card per lever: name, one-line definition, an Indian example and a 'used on you' line. Level 1: scarcity, social proof, FOMO, anchoring. Level 2: charm pricing, loss aversion, the free effect, reciprocity. Level 3: decoy effect, paradox of choice, halo effect, framing. Level 4: mere exposure, commitment bias, endowment effect, bandwagon. All 16 cards are transcribed in full in the brain. Gate: 'comment MKT' for the slides; not needed, the frames carried everything.
items.use: A 16-row checklist on every client ad brief: which ONE lever does this ad pull, and at which second? (a client product ads are mostly social proof + anchoring + a festival-window scarcity; a client is halo + endowment.) For KaalAurKatha titles, pinned comments and captions, the honest levers are framing and commitment ('Day 7 of 11'); social-proof numbers only when true.

items.title: Meta ads reel (could not download)
items.teaches: Download failed twice on 2026-10-26: Instagram returned an empty media response for this reel, which means it is private, deleted, or only visible when logged in. The worker never logs in to Instagram. If the reel is public for you, re-share it or share a different link to the same video; if it is from a private account, it cannot be fetched.

items.title: Three ways to start music naturally: reversed ending, stem cut, riser + whoosh
items.creator: @iam_ar_un
items.teaches: Instead of hard-starting the music at the playhead, put a lead-in on the track below that ends exactly on the music's first downbeat. Three versions shown on a Premiere timeline: (1) End cut reversed: the song's own last 2–3 s, reversed, swelling into bar one. (2) The stem cut: one instrument stem of the same song plays a bar or two, then the full mix drops. (3) Riser & whoosh: a riser/transition SFX plus a deep whoosh and a mid whoosh with fade curves that crescendo into the downbeat. All three are buildable headless with ffmpeg; the node has the commands and a frame/envelope verifier plan for Phase 2.
items.use: The music entry on cinematic cuts, as you asked: the Raktabeej teaser at the moment the title card hits, a client ad at the first product reveal, the first beat after a katha's cold open. Default to riser + whoosh for AI-video teasers; use the reversed ending when the bed is our own Gemini track (we have the full file).

items.title: Type hierarchy from one base size × one ratio (golden-ratio type scale)
items.creator: @aevyvideoschool
items.teaches: Stop sizing each line by eye. Pick one base size (demo: 200 pt), then multiply or divide by one ratio for every other level: 200 × 1.618 = 323.6 pt above, 200 / 1.618 = 123.61 pt below. The ratio sets the feel: 1.618 golden = premium/luxury, 1.414 silver = modern/tech UI, 1.333 = friendly posters and H1–H2, 1.25 = soft buttons and body, 1.2 = subtle editorial. One error on the card: 1.25 is the major third, not the perfect fifth (1.5). Demo poster rebuilt live in Photoshop.
items.use: Every design with text: ChatGPT cover prompts phrase it as proportions (subline about 60% of the headline height, since the model ignores pt sizes); kaalaurkatha.com and Pocket Ledger get a CSS type scale with one --ratio variable, and any off-scale font size is a review flag; a client layouts pick the ratio from the brand vibe first. Example: a 1080-wide KaalAurKatha cover on a 1.618 scale from a 120 px headline is 120 → 74 → 46.

items.title: Five viral background songs by vibe (Now or Never, ELBM, Evergreen, Daisies, Runaway)
items.creator: @maxcreates.mp4
items.teaches: A music-only reel: five song clips scroll past on a Premiere timeline, each tagged with a vibe. Now or Never = Motivational, ELBM = Storytelling, Evergreen (tiktok) = Hopeful, Daisies = Vibey/Happy, Runaway = Dramatic. Caption says all five are on YouTube; add 'instrumental' to the search for a no-vocals version. They are commercial tracks, so on YouTube long-form they draw Content ID claims; the useful part is the vibe map as a reference for describing the feel to Gemini when we generate our own bed.
items.use: Music placement on a tutorial or explainer cut (Cutaway channel narration, a fitness-page tutorial reel): pick the vibe from this five-way map, then describe that feel to Gemini for a free, claim-safe bed instead of using the track. Example: a 'hopeful' Cutaway explainer bed described as slow fingerpicked acoustic with a soft build.

items.title: Roast Room: seven AI advisors (Bezos, Buffett, Hormozi...) debate a business decision inside Claude Code
items.creator: @nateherkai
items.teaches: GitHub nateherkai/roast-room (893 stars): each advisor is a Claude agent built from that person's public videos, letters and books (Hormozi: 124 videos, 1.3M words). You type /roast-room "Should I raise my prices?", Claude picks the advisors, a local web UI runs Brief → Openings → Fault lines → Debate → Vote → Verdict, forces a devil's advocate if they agree too fast, scores every option and gives a PDF. /newroaster adds anyone. Nothing installed, code not read (it has a web app and .env keys).md, costs every chat). OK with Always, or With its pack (fires only in tool/app tasks)?
items.use: Devil's advocate for real decisions: a new channel format, a client's pricing, whether Pocket Ledger goes public, the Cutaway launch. Add Indian creators/operators as roasters. On Keep: read all its code first, install hidden (skillOverrides), list in its pack; if Always, one trigger line in CLAUDE.md core.

items.title: The 20-item "don't get sued" legal checklist to run on every app and site before launch
items.creator: @krishanu.builds (Krishanu Mahapatra)
items.teaches: One checklist to paste into Claude before any launch: privacy policy, terms, refund and cookie policies, cookie banner, form consents, data minimisation, third-party SDK audit, no dark patterns, hidden fees, fake reviews or unsupported claims, alt text, colour contrast, keyboard navigation, business details, age consent for kids' data, unsubscribe link, licensed fonts and images, data deletion requests. Full list is in the caption, nothing gated. For India this maps onto the DPDP Act 2023 and the e-commerce rules; add a grievance officer contact and GST identity. Not legal advice.
items.use: A pre-deploy legal pass on kaalaurkatha.com and the Pocket Ledger app (bank-SMS ingest needs the data items most), run as one prompt right before the 20-item performance pass from 25 Oct.

items.title: Three GitHub repos for code-rendered video with Opus 5.5: P(doom) music video, Awesome Opus Videos, Lemo-Opuscar (59 film styles)
items.creator: @aiwithaddy
items.teaches: Three repos, read from the README frames: (1) "I'm Upping My P(doom)", a music video where every frame is a deterministic function of song time, with word-level lyric alignment (Demucs + forced alignment + Whisper). (2) "Awesome Opus 5.5 Videos", 418 viral code-made videos each with the prompt used (HTML, Canvas, SVG, Three.js). (3) "Lemo-Opuscar" (lemonno-ai), 59 film styles made in code, MIT + CC BY 4.0, 7.2K stars, incl. 8 "Evidence Films" styles that film real material with every number sourced. Links gated behind "comment Opus"; nothing cloned or run.
items.use: Same lane as our HyperFrames motion-graphics skills (code, not AI video). On Keep: read Lemo-Opuscar's Evidence Films styles and port one into a HyperFrames composition for a KaalAurKatha facts reel or a Cutaway explainer; use the P(doom) word-alignment model for our caption pass. Awesome-Opus is a prompt gallery, reference only.

items.title: Endless Tools: browser app that stacks effects on footage, images, text and 3D (template gallery)
items.creator: @antonmehto
items.teaches: A web app (@endlesstools) where you upload footage, an image, text or a 3D object and stack mix-and-match effects on it: the demo shows a chromatic liquid smear and a bloom pass. It also has a gallery of "customizable, art-directed templates" (Background, Illustration, Key Visual, Logo, Typography). The link is gated behind "comment Tool" and never shown, so nothing was opened; pricing and export unknown. Everything it demos EffectCraft and HyperFrames already do at zero credits, so its value is the template gallery as a look reference.
items.use: One browser look at its template gallery before a client key visual or a site hero (same role as prompt-motion.com): borrow the look, build it in EffectCraft or HyperFrames. Not a pipeline tool.

items.title: Pixel-icon kinetic monologue (paper type, thermal silhouette, icon ring, word spelled by icons) + its 5-line script shape
items.creator: @jordans.archivess (Jordan Watkins)
items.teaches: A 20 s spoken monologue illustrated with zero AI: bold grotesque type on off-white paper, 16-bit pixel icons that burst into a rotating ring, a real person turned into a thermal-camera silhouette, red marker loops, and the last word LOVE spelled out one letter at a time with an icon standing in for each letter. The script has a fixed shape: question → "You don't." → "You just show it." → three abstract nouns → one closing phrase ending on a single spellable word. Node page has every beat with timestamps, the EffectCraft build and a worked example of writing a new script the same way.
items.use: KaalAurKatha facts reel or channel trailer: a new 5-line script in this shape (e.g. "How do you know a story is true? / You don't. / You just carry it. / Through memory, ritual, doubt, / through one's own need to..."), pixel icons drawn from the episode's props, the deity silhouette as the thermal plate. Also a a client process reel with the maker's hands as the thermal shot.

items.title: getdesign.md: drop a big brand's design system into a project as DESIGN.md
items.creator: @codernormie
items.teaches: getdesign.md hosts DESIGN.md analyses of ~70 brands (Spotify, Apple, Stripe, Linear, Figma...): colours with roles, type, buttons, cards, forms. npx getdesign@latest add spotify writes spotify/DESIGN.md into the project; you tell the coding agent to read it before writing any UI. Site calls them inspiration, not a licence. Not run; package code not read.
items.use: kaalaurkatha.com and the Pocket Ledger app: pull one close reference (Spotify for dark media UI, Linear for the ledger) as a starting DESIGN.md, then rewrite into our own tokens. Bigger takeaway: keep a DESIGN.md in every web project so each session reads one file before touching UI.

items.title: Paper-cutout brand promo (cream paper type, red paper cut-outs, marker handwriting, macro metaphor B-roll)
items.creator: @jordans.archivess (Jordan Watkins)
items.teaches: An 82 s sponsored promo built from three materials: cream paper carrying the type (grotesque captions + a Didone italic for one precious word + red marker handwriting), red paper carrying physical cut-outs placed stop-motion, and the real room dressed in the same red and cream. Every graphic gets a physical twin (the word Software becomes a sticker held to the lens). Chess macro as metaphor B-roll; whip-pan, VHS rainbow smear, neon flicker and scanner sweep as the only transitions. Median shot 1.8 s.
items.use: brandaurkatha client promos (a client, a client product lines): the product and its benefits as paper cut-outs on brand-colour paper, red marker accents, one macro metaphor. Also a KaalAurKatha channel trailer or 'how we make an episode' reel.

items.title: Mixed-media collage kinetic type (grain paper, duotone portrait, neon word, paper panels)
items.creator: @johnbucog
items.teaches: A 24 s promo where every cut is a different material: grained dark paper, a solarised cyan duotone of the speaker with glitch blocks, huge condensed headline words popping on each spoken beat, a red neon word, flat red/cyan paper panels, red marker scribbles, RGB-smear transitions. Median shot 0.7 s. Steps, timestamps and our EffectCraft build are on the node page. The reel's content (LTX Trainer: train a style model instead of prompting) is a separate untested method note.
items.use: Short-form hooks: a KaalAurKatha facts reel or channel trailer where the headline words slam on-beat over a duotone of the deity plate; or a a client process reel with the maker's portrait in duotone. Too loud for the itihas long form.

items.title: Agent Reach: one CLI that lets an agent search Reddit, Twitter, YouTube, GitHub with no API fees
items.creator: @codernormie
items.teaches: GitHub iqjiy/agent_reach (~87k stars on screen, MIT, Chinese README): opencli commands that read and search Twitter, Reddit, YouTube, GitHub, Bilibili, XiaoHongShu through your browser logins, returning only matches so Claude burns fewer tokens. Demo: Claude runs opencli reddit search on his niche. Not installed, code not read. Overlaps Apify and our local yt-dlp path; new bit is free Reddit/Twitter search for trends.
items.use: Trends and discovery research in youtube_story (what Reddit/Twitter say about a topic before an episode brief) at zero cost. If you Keep it: I read the whole repo first, install outside Drive in its own venv, and never point it at Instagram.

items.title: Moving Image Archive: free public-domain footage, searched by describing the shot
items.creator: @sneha_sidequest
items.teaches: movingimagearchive.com (by Cole @covacut, free): 100,000+ public-domain clips from 1894 to 2021, cut into single shots and matched with CLIP, so you type "san francisco, 1906" instead of tags. Every clip has a provenance/rights panel. Not opened yet; download format and rights-for-India unchecked.
items.use: Footage source in the asset-manifest step of any KaalAurKatha episode or facts reel that touches the last ~130 years (freedom movement, old city streets, trains, temples on film), and period B-roll for the Cutaway channel. Not for mythological episodes.

items.title: The 20-item "make my vibe-coded site fast" prompt (ends with a Lighthouse audit)
items.creator: @joshtheaiguy
items.teaches: One prompt to Claude listing every standard web performance fix: compress images, lazy loading, code splitting, cache API responses, CDN, minify JS/CSS, index the database, cut unnecessary re-renders, debounce input handlers, paginate large lists, remove unused dependencies, defer non-critical scripts, loading skeletons, load balancer, compress API payloads, DB connection pooling, cache expensive computed results, fix N+1 queries, server-side caching, then a Lighthouse audit. Caption: Claude does not optimise for scale by default, especially with Supabase. The full table is in the brain.
items.use: A pre-ship performance pass for kaalaurkatha.com (front-end + delivery items only, it is static Astro) and the Pocket Ledger app, run as one prompt and verified by Lighthouse.

items.title: Google ARTEMIS: open-source agent that drives a real Android phone from plain English (MCP for Claude Code)
items.creator: @jagu.builds
items.teaches: ARTEMIS (google/artemis on GitHub, Apache 2.0, ~14k stars per the reel) lets an AI agent operate a real Android phone or emulator from plain English, e.g. uv run artemis run "Open Settings, find Battery and tell me the current level". It ships an MCP server (mobile_run_task, mobile_get_device_state, mobile_inspect_trace, mobile_diagnose) and uv run artemis mcp --install all wires it into Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and more. Flash mode is a fast reactive loop (3–5 s a step); Pro mode is planner + operator + checker (15–40 s a step). The 99.1% AndroidWorld score is Google's own, self-reported. Nothing installed.
items.use: Automated QA of the Pocket Ledger app on your own Pixel: build, install, log in with a test account, tap every screen, catch popups, screenshot everything. The Android counterpart of the iOS Simulator tool we already have.

items.title: MiroFish: a synthetic focus group of AI people that argues about your idea before you build
items.creator: @nick_saraev
items.teaches: MiroFish is an open-source simulation engine (the reel claims 80k GitHub stars; demo at 666ghj.github.io/mirofish-demo). You upload a pitch, idea doc or rough MVP as PDF/MD/TXT; it builds a graph of simulated people with personalities and opinions, drops them on a simulated social platform, lets them argue, then writes a report on why they loved or hated it and what to change, and you can chat with any single agent. It is a synthetic focus group, not real users: good for finding objections and fixing messaging before launch, never proof of demand. Gatekept CTA (comment STARTUP) not followed.
items.use: At the end of each build stage of kaalaurkatha.com or the Pocket Ledger app: feed the pitch and screenshots, read the objections, fix the copy before going public. Also a cheap pre-test for a client ad concept with the brief and script as seeds.

items.title: /brag: one Claude Code command turns a project into a 20-second launch video (HyperFrames)
items.creator: @codernormie
items.teaches: /brag (github.com/latent-spaces/brag, MIT) is a Claude Code plugin: one command turns the site or app you just built into a 20-second launch video with music, motion and share copy, rendered with HyperFrames. Install is two plugin commands (marketplace add latent-spaces/brag, then install brag@brag); it adds /brag and /brag-slim, and letsbrag.app renders the same from a pasted URL with no install. He demoed it on his founder-ideas site. We already have HyperFrames and the hidden product-launch-video skill, so this is a candidate to compare, not a gap. Not installed.
items.use: A 20-second launch reel for kaalaurkatha.com, the Pocket Ledger app or a client's site/app, for IG and the portfolio. On Keep: read its code, run it on the site repo, judge it against our own product-launch-video skill; install hidden only if it wins.

items.title: Shannon: open-source AI pentester for web apps and APIs
items.creator: @codernormie
items.teaches: Shannon (github.com/KeygraphHQ/shannon) is an open-source AI pentester for web apps and APIs, authorised testing only. He points Claude Code at the repo ("setup this repo in this directory"), picks the AI provider (he used his ChatGPT subscription), runs it without Docker, then gives it the live URL plus the source folder. It runs a pentest pipeline (Temporal workflow) over injection, auth, authz and SSRF classes and writes a report; his 5-second demo shows the dashboard, not a real finding. Nothing installed; its code must be read first.
items.use: Pre-launch security pass on our own deployed sites only: kaalaurkatha.com and the Pocket Ledger app (its Apps Script ingest endpoint), run against our URL + our repo, after the free built-in /security-review. Same family as the 25 Oct security-skills list; pick one, not all.

items.title: Meta ads budget scaling: +20% every 3 days, never double
items.creator: @dukaandari.tv
items.teaches: A Hinglish two-character sketch (Ads ka Hisaab #02). Doubling a Meta ad budget in one jump (₹2,000→₹4,000) gave 6→7 orders, cost per order ₹333→₹571, because the ad re-enters learning and the extra money buys pricier people. Rule: raise 20%, wait 3 days, check orders, repeat; stop at the first step that adds budget but no orders; if ROAS falls, drop back one step. Bonus: those two weeks reveal the winning creative, so next time launch it straight at the plateau budget. Gatekept: comment SCALE for a planner (not fetched). Example numbers are illustrative, not data.
items.use: The first paid-media note in the brain. Use it the day we put money behind anything: boosting a KaalAurKatha reel, or a brandaurkatha client asking to scale a working ad. Step +20% per 3 days, log cost per result per step, stop at the plateau, roll back one step on a ROAS drop, relaunch the winning creative at the plateau budget. Craft note: the dialogue-plus-data-board format is a good model for a numbers-driven Hinglish explainer series.

items.title: Top 10 Claude/Codex security skills (list, not installed)
items.creator: @brochbuilds
items.teaches: A music-only listicle of 10 GitHub security skills for Claude Code/Codex (Cloudflare Security Audit, Trail of Bits, Anthropic's Defending Code, CC Safety Net, AgentGuard and more). Full table in the brain. None verified or installed: a third-party skill gets full access to the Mac and costs context in every chat. We already have built-in /security-review for free.

Only if that misses things, read the code of #4 CC Safety Net (blocks destructive commands and .env leaks, useful now that the hourly worker runs unattended) and #3 Anthropic Defending Code, then decide.

items.title: Stop saving reels: share to Recall, triage the old pile with Claude
items.creator: @anas.helloworld
items.teaches: New reels: share to the Recall app instead of saving (it transcribes them, so they're searchable). Floating clones: rotoscoped high-frame-rate jumps, scaled down, keyframed upward, foreground re-cut on top
Recolour one part of a subject (a black dress to red/green/blue) with Roto Brush + a solid on Lighten + a Multiply copy
Replace a green laptop screen with Mocha AE corner pin + a Keylight hand matte so fingers stay in front
Surreal building slide: tracked mask cuts one face of a building, a pre-comp of it is tiled with CC RepeTile and keyframed upward so the building slides past itself
Documentary war-map redesign: one colour theme, 3D falling bomb, article match cut, inverted B&W satellite map with explosions
Mixed-media collage kinetic type (grain paper, duotone portrait, neon word, paper panels)
3D path carousel: clips glide in a ribbon along a pen-drawn S-curve, driven by two expressions and a Progress slider
Pendulum light logo reveal: a swinging bulb whose glow lights up the logo (India's Got Latent S2 opener)
Pixel-icon kinetic monologue (paper type, thermal silhouette, icon ring, word spelled by icons)
Profile bounce: a screenshot (Instagram profile) cut into ~14 element layers that bounce in one after another with an inertial-bounce expression
Shard character intro: a cut-out portrait split into 5 tilted rectangular shards (one mask per layer, white Stroke edge) over a red radial card and a rough-edged gradient name title
Texturize paper relief, a hidden paper scan embossed into the tape, the text and the background so a collage motion graphic looks printed on real paper
Gradient shimmer text: a blurred, turbulent colour map pushed through the type with CC Blobbylize, then threshold + cross blur + glow
Cosmic chrome text: a 5-colour palette mapped through a bevel/depth normal (angle, contrast, bulge, rounding), animated by Phase, finished with Deep Glow
Finger point tracking: one Motion Tracker per fingertip, stop at 95% confidence, data onto Null objects
The Speed effect: the subject is rotoscoped off a clean background plate and keyframed out of frame in 6 frames with motion blur, so they "zip" away
FilmCraft techniques
Object hits a subject, bounces back and drops, built from three stacked Transform effects with motion blur
"Voice over music: duck the song with two effects (level −20…−30 dB, a wide −11.5 dB dip at 2168.5 Hz, Lowpass 2.5 kHz), so narration or dialogue sits in front"
Voice pocket on the music (compress only the speech band of the background score, so narration cuts through while the music stays loud)
Beat-sync background flicker: subject cut-out over a 0.1 s landscape montage, revealed by a rotating mirror mask
Reaction cutaway over a dialogue join (overlap the two audio takes, lay the listener's expression shot on top so the jump is never seen)
Cinematic look library, the finishing grade for every KaalAurKatha AI video (soft film tone + 9 named looks, values measured from the reel's frames)
Colour splash: one subject stays in colour, everything else desaturated (duplicate clip + subject cut-out on top, saturation down on the base)

Grade any camera's log clip: pick the camera and its log profile (input transform), then a creative look, then a split tone (ToneLab Chroma in Premiere, rebuilt with FilmCraft's built-in camera LUTs); plus how to get a log-style AI clip and grade it back

Log to final, nine before/after scenarios (daylight city, blue-hour summit, hard-light alley, sunset sea, shrine, fireworks, sun through clouds, autumn park, autumn garden), each measured into a recipe
Neon Glow look: Find Edges (Invert) → Tint white-to-cyan → VR Glow, turns any shot into glowing neon line art
Paper-cutout brand promo (cream paper type, red paper cut-outs, marker handwriting, metaphor macro B-roll)
Slow Shutter effect: Echo (8 echoes, Maximum) + Posterize Time 12 fps for a dreamy smeared-trail look
Freeze-frame character intro: frame-hold segment, masked cut-out on top, 4-colour-gradient matte behind, soft-light overlay, name + role title
Flash Whip transition: a 2-frame white silhouette of the incoming subject over the outgoing shot, then a whip from below
Gangsta extract transition: vertical blur + luma invert + Extract (threshold) on a ~5-frame adjustment layer
Ink transition: a black-on-white ink-bleed overlay used as a reversed Luma Track Matte on clip B
Invert Chromatic transition: 3–6-frame inverted + RGB-split hits on short adjustment clips over a B&W edit
"Opium stretch effect (his \"OPM effect\"): a 13-frame horizontal Stretch transition on the cut under a ~10-frame Noise + Extract adjustment layer"
Prism Lens transition: a 14-frame window (last 12 of A + first 2 of B), each nested, dropped into a two-slot transition comp with a prism/light-leak smear
Radial shutter transition: edge-only directional blur + 2-frame Linear Dodge flash
Rapid Zoom Out: a burst of 3-frame photos, each zooming 200 → 100 with Transform shutter-angle blur, in black and white
Shutter Slide: a stair-step stack of 10-frame photos, each dropping in from above with Transform shutter-angle blur
Thermal Grunge transition: a ~1 s thermal-camera stinger (heat-map LUT + Posterize Time + halftone/paper textures, nested) between two shots
X-Ray Transition: a cut that flashes through a negative frame and an AI "X-ray / wireframe" still of the subject
